---
title: "Technical details"
---

This article explains how altdown builds a site. altdown doesn't render
anything itself: [altdoc](https://altdoc.etiennebacher.com/) converts the man
pages and vignettes and renders them with Quarto, and altdown supplies the
[pkgdown](https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/)-style layout around them.

## How a build works

`altdown::build_site()` runs in three stages:

1. **Before rendering**, it writes a set of files into `altdoc/`. altdoc copies
   that folder into its Quarto project, so these files end up in the site.
2. **During rendering**, `altdoc::render_docs()` converts the Rd files to
   Quarto pages and renders the project. A pre-render script fixes up the man
   pages before Quarto sees them.
3. **After rendering**, it adds hover tooltips to the HTML in `docs/`.

Customizing a site by generating its source files and then calling
`altdoc::render_docs()` is the approach altdoc itself recommends for
Quarto[^customize].

[^customize]: See altdoc's
    [customization vignette](https://altdoc.etiennebacher.com/articles/customize.html).

The only file you edit is `altdoc/altdown.yml`. Everything else in `altdoc/` is
rewritten on every build, and gitignored by `altdown::use_altdown()`:

```text
altdoc/
├── altdown.yml                # configuration, edited by hand
├── quarto_website.yml         # Quarto configuration (navbar, footer, theme)
├── index.md                   # home page
├── reference.qmd              # function reference index
├── authors.qmd                # authors and citation page
├── altdown.scss               # pkgdown-style theme on top of Quarto's HTML
├── altdown-header.html        # dark-mode default
├── altdown-after-body.html    # navbar alignment
└── altdown-pre-render.R       # fixes up altdoc's man pages
```

## Before rendering

### The home page

altdoc's home page is an `index.md` that includes `README.md`. altdoc copies
`altdoc/` into its Quarto project after importing the README, so the
`altdoc/index.md` that `build_site()` writes takes its place. It holds the
README's content next to a pkgdown-style sidebar, with links, the license, the
citation, the developers and the README's badges.

The sidebar is a `.column-margin` div, Quarto's margin column, so on a narrow
screen it moves below the content as Quarto's layout intends. The README's
title and body share one div, so text wraps around a logo floated in the
title.

A README image can have a light and a dark version, given GitHub's way, as a
`<picture>` with a `<source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)">`. On the site
that would follow the operating system's setting instead of the site's own
light/dark toggle, so each such `<picture>` becomes one `<img>` per theme, using
Quarto's `.light-content` and `.dark-content` classes.

### The reference index

altdoc has no way to group and order the function index, like pkgdown's
`reference:` field
([etiennebacher/altdoc#326](https://github.com/etiennebacher/altdoc/issues/326)).
So `altdoc/altdown.yml` has a `reference:` field of its own, in the same shape
as pkgdown's:

```yaml
reference:
  - title: Building the site       # <1>
    desc: >                        # <2>
      Set up a package, then build its site.
    contents:
      - use_altdown                # <3>
      - starts_with("build_")      # <4>
```
1. Each entry becomes a section of the index, with this heading.
2. An optional description, shown under the heading.
3. A topic, by any of its `\alias{}` names.
4. A selector, as in pkgdown: `starts_with()`, `ends_with()`, `contains()`,
   `matches()`, `has_concept()`, `has_keyword()`, `-` to exclude and `c()` to
   combine.

`build_site()` resolves these against the `\name{}` and `\alias{}` entries in
`man/*.Rd` and writes the index to `altdoc/reference.qmd`.

### The navbar and footer

`altdoc/quarto_website.yml` is generated in full. The navbar links the "Get
started" vignette, the reference index, the other vignettes under "Articles" and
the changelog. The footer has pkgdown's "Developed by ..." text, built from
`Authors@R`.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Changing the Quarto configuration

A `quarto:` field in `altdown.yml` is merged over the generated configuration.
A list of entries, like the navbar's items, is added to; any other setting is
replaced, and `~` removes it. For example, to add a link to the navbar and fold
code blocks:

```yaml
quarto:
  website:
    navbar:
      right:
        - text: Blog
          href: https://example.com
  format:
    html:
      code-fold: true
```
:::

## During rendering: the man pages

altdoc converts each `man/*.Rd` file to a `.qmd` page during
`altdoc::render_docs()` and renders the Quarto project straight after, so
`build_site()` can't edit those pages beforehand. Instead,
`altdown-pre-render.R` runs as a Quarto pre-render script, inside that render.
It makes the pages look like pkgdown's:

- **Usage** becomes an R code block, so it's syntax-highlighted and gets a copy
  button, like the examples.
- **Inline code** becomes Markdown code spans. Pandoc would otherwise turn a `"`
  inside `<code>` into a curly quote, and a trailing backslash would escape the
  closing `</code>`.
- **Examples** that are run show their output in the same block, prefixed with
  `#>`. The `library()` call altdoc adds for the package itself is hidden.
- **Examples that aren't run** (`\dontrun{}`) become plain code blocks, so their
  pages render without starting an R session[^knitr].

[^knitr]: A ```` ```{r} ```` chunk makes Quarto render the page with knitr, even
    with `eval=FALSE`, and that starts a separate R session per page.

## After rendering: hover tooltips

Quarto's `code-link` option links function names in code blocks to their
documentation with downlit, but downlit doesn't know about this site, so it
can't link the package's own functions to their man pages here. So after
rendering, `build_site()` goes through every
page in `docs/` and links each reference to one of the package's own functions,
in a code block or in inline code, to its man page. Hovering over it shows a
tooltip with the function's usage and the first sentence of its description,
taken from `man/*.Rd`.

Try it: hover over `build_site()` or `use_altdown()`. To build without
tooltips, use `build_site(tooltips = FALSE)`.

::: {.callout-note}
The tooltip shows the first sentence of the description, cut off at 200
characters. `build_site()` warns when a sentence is longer, so you can shorten
it.
:::

## Matching the pkgdown look

`altdown.scss` is a Quarto theme layer, added on top of Quarto's own light and
dark themes:

```yaml
theme:
  light: [default, altdown.scss]
  dark: [darkly, altdown.scss]
```

It is based on pkgdown's `pkgdown.scss`, with the selectors adapted to Quarto's
HTML. It:

- limits the navbar to a centered, fixed-width container;
- puts the navbar items (title, links, search, GitHub icon) in pkgdown's order;
- styles the margin sidebar and the reference index to look like pkgdown's.

Two things can't be done in CSS alone:

- **Dark mode by default.** Quarto's light/dark toggle always starts new
  visitors on the light theme. `altdown-header.html` starts them on the dark
  theme if their system prefers it, unless they've used the toggle before.
- **Aligning the navbar title with the body text.** Quarto's home page uses a
  different layout from the other pages, so the body's left edge isn't in the
  same place on every page. `altdown-after-body.html` measures it once the page
  has loaded and adjusts the navbar's padding to match.
